correctness.rationale: Start from previously proved W=kappa(H)+kappa(complement H)-2. Exact hypergeometric isolated-vertex probabilities are n times two binomial ratios. Uniform edge-cut sampling without replacement bounds any two-isolate or non-singleton-component exception by O(n^2 4^-n); it also bounds Pr(W>=2) and the expectation error by O(n^3 4^-n). Expanding the fixed-edge hypergeometric product with explicit first three power sums cancels the relative n^-1 term and produces the 1/3 coefficient. Averaging the two near-half edge counts adds 2/n^2 exactly when N is odd. The self-contained verifier from the actual package replayed its recorded output; 359423 small balanced assignments and n<=300 asymptotic cases corroborate boundaries but are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 equitable complete-graph model had only a qualitative vanishing expectation. The exact leading rare-event mechanism, exponential suppression of multiple wild edges, and the nonzero parity-sensitive second-order coefficient give quantitative information needed for rare-failure probabilities of minimal colour-connectivity repair. The cancellation of the entire 1/n relative term and the parity bifurcation are structurally invisible in a routine connectivity-to-one statement. The object and invariant have an established direct combinatorial interpretation.
